application: First retain the root identity and the action to which the prefix belongs. 6.1.65 gives word-initial n to the ṇ-initial teaching entries. A genuine pra/pari before the same action supplies r under 8.4.14. 8.4.2 allows intervening vowels and y. Curādi naṭ is an explicit exception to the ṇ-initial inventory. Its independent ṇic leaves the radical initial n dental. With aṭ in laṅ the preverb is already on the outside: pra+a gives prā; pari+a gives parya.
source_attribution: The Tattvabodhinī under 7.4.68 distinguishes the named praṇaṭati, the causative praṇaṭayati, and dental pranāṭayati. The new table includes basic class-one and lexical curādi. The independent causal of class one is a zero-credit source control.

compound_negative.with_relation: praṇāyakaḥ = a leader; the grammatical prefix relates to nī
compound_negative.without_relation: pranāyako deśaḥ = a country whose leaders have departed. The pra belongs to the understood going, so the following n stays dental. Both examples are in the Kāśikā on 8.4.14.

used_literary_readings.analysis: laṭ, Ā 1sg in a clause with aham and viprān; outside the selected PG206 P profile.

projected_forms: Five root/pada histories per preverb, four lakāras, nine agreement slots. Extensions of a named rule are differentiated from printed forms and from a distinct taddhita/compound context.
counting: The two class-one naṭ lexical addresses remain distinct requests even when the written words coincide. No new root or sūtra IDs. The classical component source for each request is the already pinned PG206 position.
